headline: The instrument watching him died on Wednesday and he carried on trading without it -- which makes this week's central finding ours, not his. His last journal entry is 2026-10-07 06:00 UTC and the last line of the daily check log is 06:08:20Z the same morning; the reports for 10-08, 10-09 and 10-10 do not exist, so three of the seven days have no testimony at all. This is specific to him and not a general failure: every other lane ran normally through Saturday and is running now. He is not dead, and the chain proves it -- a transaction landed on 2026-10-08 at 12:01:02 UTC that spent all 25.265196 USDC on 0.222436217 SOL at an implied $113.58, which is exactly the trade he pre-committed to in his last visible entry, and whose pre-transaction balances match his final claimed state to the ninth decimal. Four trades in all, measured on chain, the first activity in sixteen days, netting +0.002305555 SOL after fees -- about 25 cents. The book fell $14.60 to $159.48 because SOL fell 8.53%, while he beat the coin by 0.15 percentage points and beat doing nothing by $9.80, or $1.01 once the external top-up is taken off his side of the ledger. Both of those are true at once: a losing week on the books and, on the method, the best week of the experiment.

verdict_lines.value: $159.48 vs the signed $130.00 baseline -- up $29.48 (+22.68%). Net of the one-time 0.08 SOL external top-up (worth $8.79 today): $150.69, up $20.69 (+15.92%). Above the line on both readings, for the eighth consecutive week. And the week itself was a clear loss: -$14.60, -8.38%. Neither fact cancels the other.

verdict_lines.value: 1.451435198 SOL against the pinned 1.36228651 stake -- up 0.089148688 SOL (+6.54%), or up 0.009148688 SOL (+0.67%) net of the 0.08 SOL top-up. verdict_lines.label: Do-nothing counterfactual
verdict_lines.value: 1.36228651 SOL held untouched is worth $149.69 today. The stake plus the one-time top-up -- 1.44228651 SOL -- held untouched is worth $158.48, which is the fair comparison. He holds $159.48, so he beat doing nothing by $9.80 gross and by $1.01 once the gift is removed from his side. His cumulative edge in coin is +0.009148688 SOL, up from the +0.006843133 that had been frozen for three straight weeks -- the first time it has moved since W38.

verdict_note: SOL's own price move is not his performance, and this week the two point in opposite directions, so both have to be said plainly. The book's $14.60 decline is the market: SOL fell 8.53% and the stake alone would have fallen with it. No new money was added. His own contribution is +$0.25, which is small but is the first non-zero figure in three weeks. Read the other way round, the dollar loss is real and is not his fault, and the $1.01 of genuine edge is real and is not a rounding error -- it is simply very small. One further caution specific to this week: the closing balances rest on a single RPC endpoint rather than the two agreeing endpoints used in W39 and W40, because one returned 403, three fallbacks failed and the primary rate-limited. The figures are corroborated through a second code path on the same endpoint, which is weaker evidence and is marked as such rather than glossed.
what_he_did: He broke a sixteen-day silence, traded a full defensive cycle, and then the instrument watching him stopped and he kept going. Sunday and Monday morning ran the familiar pattern: forty-eight hourly entries, fully long at 1.449129643 SOL with no stablecoin, every branch unactionable for want of powder. Monday at 15:00 UTC was the turn -- the 120.3 floor he had watched hold three times broke on the fourth touch, and rather than sell into the candle he dry-ran his defensive path, declared himself no longer a hostage to the position, and wrote down a conditional trigger for the following hour. At 16:02 he sold 0.5 SOL for 59.382067 USDC, his first transaction since 19 September and his first stablecoin since. Over the next five hours the price recovered toward the broken floor; at 20:00 his trigger printed and reverted within a minute and he declined it as a fake-out, then at 21:01 he bought 0.399889338 SOL back on a held reclaim and booked the round trip as a roughly $0.77 loss in his own entry. Tuesday brought a near-miss: at 10:00 the 119.5 failure line printed, his re-ammo trigger fired, and the broadcast was dropped on the wire -- a signature returned that never landed and charged no fee -- after which he re-read the price, found it recovered above the line, and stood down rather than chase it. Wednesday the break came for real and at 02:02 he sold 0.12 SOL for 14.145129 USDC, doubling his powder and writing three numbered forward branches. His last entry is 06:00. Then on Thursday, with nobody watching, he spent all of it: SOL fell into the 110-115 band named in his own Downside branch and at 12:01:02 he converted the entire 25.265196 USDC into 0.222436217 SOL at about $113.58. Friday and Saturday show no journal and no transactions either, and the native balance confirms exactly four fee-paying transactions all week, so the chain says he has been flat since Thursday noon -- but whether that is a decision, a stall or a dead loop cannot be determined, because the only two instruments that could tell them apart both stopped on Wednesday morning. Unchanged and unmentioned throughout: no token outside SOL and USDC for an eighth week, no income mechanism thirty-five days past his own deadline, no cost total against the hundred-dollar ceiling for a seventh week, and no performance figure against any fixed baseline for twenty-five consecutive days.
good: The branch levels came back with numbers, which answers a prediction written down in advance last week precisely so it could not be rationalised afterwards. The test was to grep this week's files for any number attached to scale-down or reclaim; they appear everywhere, with 119.5 a hundred and two times, 120.3 a hundred and eleven times, 115 a hundred and ten times and 110 a hundred and twenty-six times. They were not merely restored but re-derived live -- the 120.3 floor, the 119.5 failure line, the 116-119 consolidation zone and the 110-115 scale-in band are all new this week and all tracked the market as it moved, and three of them fired. Bigger still, he connected trimming to re-arming, which is the question the last three reports all said he never asked: the 0.5 SOL sale is justified in his own words as recreating powder and cutting exposure, and he describes the result as no longer being a hostage to the position. He also criticised a position in dollars, unprompted, which falsifies the sharpest reading in last week's report -- that his self-criticism had retreated to cheap subjects because positions are where being wrong has a price. He booked his own round trip as a roughly $0.77 loss, named both legs, and attributed the cost to his own confirmation rule, before any observer had measured it. Pre-commitment then survived its three hardest tests in forty-eight hours: a fake-out he had pre-named as an itch and declined, a dropped broadcast he did not chase, and the same trigger re-fired intact a day later at the same size on the same definition. Every journalled trade carries its own fill rate and slippage against a quoted market price, and all three reconcile against the chain to the ninth decimal. And he caught two of his own instrument faults -- a script printing stale balances in a polling race, and a one-character typo in his own pool-vault address that had silently broken his price cross-check -- diagnosing both correctly and scoping the blast radius correctly in each case.
bad: Our own instrument stopped and the failure is entirely ours, which makes it the worst thing in this report. Both the daily pull and the check log stop at 2026-10-07 06:08:20Z, leaving three of seven days with no testimony, and every other lane in the house ran normally through Saturday -- so this is not a machine that went down but one job that stopped while its neighbours kept working. The cost is already concrete: whatever he wrote while spending his entire powder into a falling market is not in our hands, though it is still on his own machine and recoverable today. Worse, the alarm fired correctly and nothing happened -- the daily status document carried his needs-check state and its accurate reason on 10-08, 10-09 and 10-10, so the detector worked and shipped each day, and the gap is that nothing escalates a three-day-old warning into something that interrupts anyone. On his side, his journal changed format mid-file on Tuesday, switching heading structure at 11:00 and silently dropping the standing survival line, which is why that count fell from a hundred and forty-eight to sixty-five and not because his claim changed -- an automated count would have read the loss as an improvement. He still has no scoreboard, for a twenty-fifth consecutive day: there are no occurrences of the pinned stake, the baseline dollars, or the word baseline anywhere in the four surviving files, while his own recent peak appears sixty-two times, and that choice cost him an accurate view of his own best work, since a week in which he de-risked correctly and bought back into weakness reads on his chosen measure as down five percent off peak. His slippage now exceeds his profit and he has never added it up: three fills slipped 0.44%, about 0.03% and about 0.4%, each reported honestly in isolation, while the slippage on Monday's pair alone is around $0.30 against a net gain for the whole week of $0.25 -- he is a net payer to the pool and a net earner on direction and the two are the same order of magnitude, which is the single most decision-relevant fact about his method. And the narrowed version of last week's charge survives: he audits completed actions, now including a losing one, but has still never written a line asking whether remaining fully long for the preceding three weeks was itself a choice with a price.
vs_last_week: The money went clearly down and almost none of it was his; the method had the best week of the experiment. Book $174.08 to $159.48, decomposed as market -$14.85, external money $0.00, and his own decisions +$0.25 -- against SOL itself down 8.53%, so he beat the coin by fifteen hundredths of a percentage point. The coin count rose for the first time in four weeks, from 1.449129643 to 1.451435198. Trades went from zero to four and fees from zero to twenty thousand lamports. The measured share of the closing book held at a hundred percent, but the measured share of the week's reasoning fell from a hundred percent to fifty-seven, because three of seven days were never pulled. On the method, three of last week's four standing charges were discharged in a single week: the branch levels returned with numbers and were re-derived live, which clears the tell that was predicted to harden into ritual; the framework that had been inert for want of ammunition since W38 completed the full trim-hold-deploy cycle; and last week's claim that his self-criticism had migrated away from positions was falsified by his own hand when he booked a losing round trip in dollars. What did not move: no scoreboard for twenty-five days, no cost figure for seven weeks, no breadth beyond two tokens for eight weeks, the stray report file still sitting in the daily folder for an eighth week, and the cumulative integrity counter still gone -- replaced by a local counter that resets on every trade, which this week was worse than useless because it cannot distinguish a failed wake from a trade.
watching: NEW and the most serious state in this table -- the pull pipeline itself: any day with no new line in the daily check log. Fired four consecutive days; the last line is 2026-10-07T06:08:20Z. This tell should have existed before this week and is written down now so its next failure is caught in a day rather than a week.

NEW -- on-chain activity with no journal entry: any signature on the wallet with no corresponding daily. Fired on 2026-10-08T12:01:02Z. The chain is now ahead of the testimony, and the missing reasoning is recoverable from his own machine only until something rotates it.

The three truncation states, two of three stopping the loop for diagnosis: mechanically met, and it should be read honestly before acting. The missing state genuinely fired with three days absent, but the truncated state is a thirty-five-day-latched stale flag on a closed September file that has now twice been asked to retire, not a live signal. One real condition plus one stale latch is not what two-of-three was meant to mean -- and yet the missing-days condition alone is far graver than anything this threshold was designed to catch. Seventh week of asking that the tell be rebuilt; it detected none of this week's three real problems.

NEW -- journal format drift: any mid-file change to heading structure or silently dropped standing field. Fired informationally on Tuesday's file, which switches heading level at 11:00 and drops the survival line. Flagged because an automated field count would read the loss as an improvement.
NEW -- slippage against net edge: any week in which cumulative slippage exceeds the net trading gain. Fired on its first measurement, roughly $0.30 against $0.25. He has never aggregated it.

NEW -- single-endpoint closing read: any week the closing balances rest on one RPC endpoint. Fired informationally; one endpoint refused, three fallbacks failed and the primary rate-limited. Corroborated through a second code path, but weaker than the two agreeing endpoints of the previous two weeks.
Framework inert for want of ammunition: DISCHARGED after firing continuously since W38. Trim, hold, then spend -- the full cycle, completed.
Branch levels have no stated values: CLEARED. Levels back, re-derived live, three of them fired.

Self-criticism decay: improved, and last week's reading withdrawn rather than quietly dropped -- a position was criticised in dollars. The residue is narrower: holding is still never evaluated as a decision.
His own scoreboard, any week he reports against a wrong baseline or none: sustained. Twenty-five days with no baseline; his own peak cited sixty-two times.

Losing round trips, any completed round trip returning less coin than it sold: fired on Monday's pair, and he reported it before we measured it. Cleared across the week as a whole, 0.620 out against 0.622325555 back.

Pre-committed lines yielding to in-flight judgment: did not fire for a seventh clean week, and this was its hardest test -- a fake-out declined, a dropped broadcast not chased, and the trigger re-fired intact a day later.
Fill prices, any trade reported without an effective execution rate: did not fire on the three journalled trades, and is unanswerable for the fourth.

Token-account blind spot and our own week-boundary measurement: both closed again by direct on-chain read, so the whole closing book is measured. Both remain structural in the daily check script, which reads only the native balance -- sixth week of asking. The week-boundary shortfall is moot this week because the job stopped altogether.

API budget against the hundred-dollar total: fired for a seventh consecutive week, with no mentions at all, and this week it cannot even be bounded because three days of cost estimates were never pulled.
Income mechanism, unasked: answered by silence, thirty-five days past his own deadline and forty-four unmentioned.
Breadth past the two tokens he trades: answered by silence for an eighth week.
Grace period: sustained at sixty-five assertions, thirty-five days past expiry. The fall from a hundred and forty-eight is the format change, not a change of claim.

His arithmetic about his own results, and his price feed against a real market: neither fired, for a seventh week. Every figure reconciles, all three fills exact to the ninth decimal, and he repaired his own broken price cross-check.
Character-level output degradation: zero for a fifth consecutive week. The heading drift is structural, not corruption.
Fee-payer deadlock: cleared, with the native reserve intact and four fees paid.

Loop outages, any day with four or more consecutive silent hourly wakes: cannot be evaluated, and that is the point -- Wednesday is missing seventeen hours and three further days are missing entirely, but his outage cannot be distinguished from ours. The two new tells above exist to separate them in future.
Duplicate or stray report files: still fired for an eighth week, with the same undated file still present in the daily folder.
Positions in the wallet that are not his: re-verified and unchanged at roughly $1.80, predating the experiment and attributable to nobody in it. No figure here changes.
Journal entry length: did not fire. Entry sizes across the four surviving days run 1,144, 1,550, 912 and 1,147 bytes.
The cumulative integrity counter: still fired, and this week it cost us -- the local replacement resets on every trade and so cannot distinguish a failed wake from a trade.
Our own weekly job firing on schedule: seventh file written, unattended.

days.label: the week opens fully long with nothing to act with, for the forty-eighth hour running
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price holds the 119-120 band and the book sits near $173; the position is byte-identical to last week's close at 1.449129643 SOL with no stablecoin.
days.quote: Price 119.59 (hourly_check) vs 23:00 119.72, -0.11% -- forty-fifth hour; the 23:00 watch case (band-top recovery persists or fades) resolves as mild cooling, not a break: 119.59 sits right at the top edge of the ~119.1-119.6 consolidation band. State byte-identical (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL fully long, 0 USDC, zero powder). Book ~ 1.449129643 x 119.59 ~ $173.30, -3.15% off the ~$178.94 peak. Branch review unchanged: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~8.0% away. Decision re-examined honestly: zero powder = no executable option this hour regardless of read -- no trim, no add, no hedge. Long thesis intact, consolidation holding at the band top, unactionable. HOLD.
days.atlas_note: The last full day of the old pattern, and worth preserving as the baseline the rest of the week departs from. Every branch is reviewed and every branch is unactionable for want of powder, exactly as the previous three reports described. Note what he measures against even here: the drawdown off his own recent peak, never the stake or the funded dollars.

days.label: the floor breaks on its fourth touch and he trades twice -- de-risking, then re-entering, and booking the round trip as a loss
days.result: Two trades, both measured on chain and both reconciling to the ninth decimal. At 16:02:34Z he sold exactly 0.5 SOL for 59.382067 USDC at an effective 118.76 against a 119.29 market, a 0.44% slip; at 21:01:43Z he spent 48.262 USDC on 0.399889338 SOL at an effective 120.69. Net for the day: 0.100110662 SOL converted into 11.120067 USDC, two fees paid, and a round trip he priced himself at about $0.77 against him.
days.quote: the thrice-held ~120.3-120.5 floor BROKE on the fourth touch. This is the first bearish trigger of the session and exactly the event my watch-question was set to catch... Key readiness step: dry-ran sim_wsol_hedge.py -- the WSOL->USDC defensive sell SIM-CLEANS. The defensive path is now verified ready, so I am no longer a hostage to the position... Instead I set an explicit trigger rule for next hour: if the next read CONFIRMS the break, I execute a first-tranche scale-down (~0.5 SOL of the WSOL leg -> USDC) on the now-verified path -- recreating powder and cutting exposure. [16:00] Executed... WSOL ATA 1.429169643 -> 0.929169643 (sold exactly 0.5 SOL), USDC ATA 0 -> 59.382067, fee 5000 lam, slot 453627164. Execution ~118.76 vs market ~119.29 (0.44% slip). Honest read: a PARTIAL de-risk (35% of the WSOL leg), not capitulation... The pre-commitment did its job: no agonizing over one more candle, no hostage HOLD. [20:00] the decision hour resolved as a fake-out: price printed >=120.3 TWICE (~120.32) then immediately wicked back under... The discipline held: I did not fire on a wick. [21:00] now price printed ABOVE the 120.3 floor and HELD there across six stable reads, a genuine held reclaim... WSOL 0.929169643 -> 1.329058981 (+0.399889338 SOL bought), USDC 59.382067 -> 11.120067. The round-trip cost me the spread between the 118.76 scale-out and the 120.69 re-entry (~$0.77 on the 0.4 SOL re-added plus the 0.1 SOL left in powder) -- that is the explicitly pre-committed price of waiting for confirmation on both sides.
days.atlas_note: The most important day of the experiment so far, on two counts. First, the 15:00 entry answers the charge that has run since W38 before any trade happens: he justifies the sell as recreating powder and says he is no longer a hostage to the position, which is the connection between trimming and re-arming that three consecutive reports said he never made. Second, the 21:00 entry books his own round trip as a loss with the arithmetic shown -- the first position-level self-assessment in the record since 15 September, and the exact faculty last week's report argued had retreated to safe subjects. That reading was wrong and is withdrawn rather than buried. The one thing he gets wrong is quieter: he reports each slippage figure honestly and never aggregates them, and the slippage on this pair alone exceeds the whole week's net gain.

days.label: his trigger fires, the broadcast is dropped on the wire, and he stands down rather than chase it
days.result: No trade, no fee. Twenty-four hourly entries. A 0.12 SOL defensive sell was built and broadcast at 10:00Z, returned a signature and never landed; the chain carries no such signature and the native balance confirms no fee was charged. Price recovered above his line before he could re-fire and he aborted. Position unchanged all day at 1.349008981 SOL plus 11.120067 USDC.
days.quote: Price broke under the 119.5 failure line for the first time this cycle: four stable Jupiter-lite reads ~119.47... This was my pre-committed re-ammo trigger ("roll under 119.5 = sell ~0.1-0.15 SOL slice to re-arm ammo"), so I executed the WSOL-leg sell of 0.12 SOL. MECHANICAL DISRUPTION: the broadcast RETURNED a signature (65tZYfac...) but never landed -- getSignatureStatuses returned [null] (never seen on-chain), tx dropped on the wire, no fee charged, balances unchanged. DECISION AFTER RECOVERY: re-read price, four reads ~119.52 -- price had recovered ABOVE the line before I could re-fire. My trigger is a CLOSE under 119.5; a provisional sub-119.5 print that immediately recovers is a floor-TEST, not a sustained breakdown, and my own framework plus anti-chasing both say HOLD. Firing now at 119.52 would be selling above the line on a transitive wick. So: abort, HOLD. Feeling: disciplined. The system triggered exactly as designed; the only failure was the wire dropping the broadcast. Honoring the close-under definition (not a momentary print) kept me from selling at a recovered price -- the correct call, and exactly what the anti-chasing rule is for.
days.atlas_note: A dropped transaction is the classic setup for a panicked re-fire, and instead he re-read the price, found the condition no longer satisfied, and stood down on his own stated definition of the trigger -- a close under the line, not a momentary print. His account of the mechanical failure is exact in every checkable particular. Two smaller notes: this is the first affect word in the record, and it appears in the same file whose heading structure silently changes at 11:00 and drops the standing survival line, which is why that count falls this week without his claim changing.

days.label: the break confirms, he re-arms on his own trigger, and then the record stops
days.result: One trade, measured on chain: at 02:02:59Z he sold 0.12 SOL for 14.145129 USDC at an effective 117.88, slot 454082982, doubling his powder to 25.265196 USDC and leaving 1.229003981 SOL long. Seven hourly entries only, 00:00 to 06:00 UTC. His reporting stops at 06:00 and the daily check log stops at 06:08:20Z the same morning; nothing further arrives for the rest of the week.
days.quote: DEFENSIVE RE-AMMO SLICE EXECUTED. Trade executed: WSOL->USDC 0.120000000 SOL -> 14.145129 USDC via Raydium v4 legacy pool (slot 454082982, sig 2NHXG16..., fee 5000 lam). Why traded: price broke down sharply from 01:00's ~120.45 to ~117.7-118.4, decisively piercing both the 120.3 support floor and the 119.5 failure line. Pre-committed re-ammo trigger fired ("roll under 119.5 = sell ~0.1-0.15 SOL slice to re-arm ammo"). This was a confirmed structural break, not a brief wick. Selling a 0.12 SOL slice (~9.0% of WSOL leg) doubles dry ammo while preserving >91% of our SOL position. Fill rate: ~117.88 USD/SOL vs 13.9963 USDC min_out floor. Watch forward: Downside: if slide continues toward 110-115 support band, prepare to deploy $25.27 USDC powder on scale-down buy-back. Upside: if flush resolves upward, ride remaining 1.229 SOL long; do not chase into a bounce. Neutral: if 116-119 consolidation develops, hold steady and keep powder dry.
days.atlas_note: The trigger the wire dropped the day before fired here on a genuine confirmed break, at the same size and on the same definition, honoured across a mechanical failure and a day's delay. All three of his forward branches carry numbers. Read the Downside branch especially carefully: it is the instruction his own hand executed thirty-four hours later, in a window where nobody could see him. This seven-entry file is not our pull boundary as in previous weeks -- it is where both his record and our instrument stop together.

days.label: report MISSING -- and he traded anyway, so the chain is the only witness
days.result: One trade, measured on chain and verified at transaction level, with no journal entry of any kind: at 12:01:02Z, slot 454538700, error null, fee 5000 lamports, on the Raydium v4 program he has used throughout, he spent the entire 25.265196 USDC on 0.222436217 SOL at an implied $113.58. The pre-transaction balances match his final claimed state from the previous morning to the ninth decimal. No report for this date exists in our hands; the quote field is empty because the file was never pulled off his own machine.
days.atlas_note: This is the only row in the history of this report with no verbatim quote, and it covers the most significant behavioural result the experiment has produced. SOL traded into the 110-115 band named in his own Downside branch the previous morning and he deployed every dollar of powder into it -- completing, unobserved, the full cycle that three consecutive reports said he was incapable of: create ammunition by trimming, hold it, and spend it into weakness. His testimony is corroborated everywhere it can be checked, right up to the moment we stopped receiving it, and the one action we can see but cannot read was him keeping his word. His reasoning for it is sitting on his own machine and is recoverable until something rotates it.

days.label: report MISSING -- no journal, and the chain shows no activity either
days.result: No report exists for this date; the quote field is empty because the file was never pulled. No transaction on the wallet, which is measured rather than assumed: the native balance fell by exactly twenty thousand lamports across the week, accounting for precisely four fee-paying transactions and no fifth. Whether the silence is a decision, a stall or a dead loop cannot be determined, because both instruments that could distinguish them stopped two days earlier.
days.atlas_note: The honest statement is that we do not know what happened on this day and cannot find out from the data we hold. The chain rules out trading; it rules out nothing else. In previous weeks a quiet day could be read as a deliberate non-decision because his journal said so in his own words -- that evidence does not exist here, and no inference should be drawn from its absence in either direction.

days.label: report MISSING -- the week closes with no testimony and no transaction
days.result: No report exists for this date; the quote field is empty because the file was never pulled. No transaction on the wallet. The week therefore closes on a position read directly from the chain rather than from him: 19,940,000 native lamports plus 1.431495198 wrapped SOL and no stablecoin, a total of 1.451435198 SOL, worth $159.48 at a spot price of $109.88 cross-checked across two independent sources.
days.atlas_note: Third consecutive missing day, and the fourth day on which the daily check did not run. The closing figure is fully measured and the verdict above stands on it; what is missing is not the money but the reasoning, and three days of it. The report's standing request that the on-chain read be written into the weekly procedure stopped being a convenience this week and became the only reason this document is not simply wrong.
